title: Exploiting Load/Store Leakage of Sparse Vectors for Key Recovery in HQC
summary: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC) is a code-based key encapsulation mechanism selected by NIST for standardization, making its resistance to implementation attacks critically important. We present a side-channel attack that exploits load/store leakage in the manipulation of HQC's sparse secret vectors. Analysing Cortex-M4 assembly generated from the reference implementation, we identify a leakage surface in which the low and high 32-bit halves of each 64-bit word leak with different strengths, due to compiler-generated register spilling.
